newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai finance minister vows fiscal discipline.
newsitem.headline: Thai finance minister vows fiscal discipline.

text.p: Thailand's acting finance minister Chaiyawat Wibulswadi on Tuesday vowed to maintain strict fiscal policy and said he would continue on the same path as the former finance minister, who resigned on Monday.

Chaiyawat, the former deputy finance minister, on Tuesday was appointed as acting finance minister by premier Banharn Silpa-archa to replace Bodi Chunnananda who suddenly stepped down on Monday. "I will cooperate with the top officials at the finance ministry, and I will continue the policies initiated by Bodi," Chaiyawat told a news conference.
Chaiyawat said he would discuss with senior officials at the finance ministry and budget bureau the possible reduction of the government budget for the fiscal year which began on October 1.
Last week, the finance ministry suggested a cut in the budget because projected revenues might not meet the 984 billion baht ($39.3 billion) spending level set for the 1996/97 financial year.
Chaiyawat said he would wait before making any moves on awarding new bank licences until the outcome of an investigation, into an alleged kickback scandal, is formally presented to cabinet.
He also said he would also continue to work to upgrade seven foreign bank offshore representative offices to full bank branches.
